sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Greenleaf Envirotech Limited; ISIN INE0PLX01017; NSE SME symbol GREENLEAF; CIN L29253GJ2010PLC059798. Incorporated 9 March 2010, public conversion 28 November 2023, NSE listing 9 October 2025. This is not Envirotech Systems or another similarly named company. Cutoff 20 October 2026; quote 19 October 2026; nominal INR five-year hurdle 15%, entry 19 October 2026 and terminal 19 October 2031. Financial amounts are crore unless explicitly rupees per share, shares, days or percentages.

Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards apply. Integrated-filing headings saying Ind AS do not override the audited accounting policy. FY26 is the first consolidated year following Greenleaf Eco Infra Private Limited's incorporation on 8 July 2025. The wholly owned subsidiary had no operating sales; FY25 consolidated comparatives are effectively parent accounts. FY21–22 come from the earlier draft restatement, FY23–25 from the final prospectus restatement, FY26 from audited consolidated statements. Original FY24–25 statutory comparisons are also preserved. This is useful history, not a completely homogeneous six-year audited panel.

G1 Hold: obtain current orders concerning the disputed RP proceedings and closure evidence for charge registration. G2 Hold: material historical comparable-restatement and subsidiary funding-classification bridges remain unresolved despite usable audited totals. FY24 CFO changes by ₹2.2185 crore between statutory and restated statements, about 97.7% of statutory PAT. Group CFO differs from parent CFO by ₹6.4297 crore, about 88.9% of group PAT; different consolidation perimeters naturally produce different totals and this difference is not itself an accounting error. The Hold concerns classification of material member deposits/capital creditors and comparability, not a fraud allegation or an assumption that group and parent cash flows must match. G3 Hold: October liquidity, revolving-line renewal and the remaining CETP funding package are unverified. G4 Conditional: exact identity, lot and eligible SM instrument are established, but missing-session status and executable depth are not.

Confidence is High for exact identity, quote, issued shares and arithmetic tied to inspected statements; Medium for financial comparability, governance assessment and operating growth; Low for attributable incremental capital economics, current funding and implementable liquidity. Missing information is not scored as a weak fact. Evidence of recurring poor cash realization is scored, while current unknown financing remains a Hold rather than a default declaration. No facts dated after 20 October are used as operating knowledge; retrieval occurred 21 October.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV5, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP NS, CASH3, BAL4, EXEC5, EARN6, R NS, D3, P5, L NS. Each is assigned once and reused. Scores 9–10 require exceptional evidence; Medium confidence limits REV to 8 despite a greater-than 30% revenue CAGR. Cheap valuation does not improve operating-quality factors.

Exact Decimal arithmetic: BQS known contribution 4.58, missing CAP weight.12, coverage.88 and missing-data bounds 4.70–5.78. GQS known contribution 5.60, missing CAP weight.15, coverage.85 and raw bounds 5.75–7.10. CASH3 is supported by repeated poor realization, including negative statutory CFO in FY24 and FY26 and supplier-supported positive FY25, so the framework's growth-quality cap 5 applies. Both post-cap mathematical endpoints are 5, but final GQS is still NS. The cap is not triggered by expansion capex itself.

IAS known contribution 1.10 from D3×.20 and P5×.10; missing Q/R/L weights total.70. Raw mathematical bounds are 1.80–8.10. Respecting the BQS dependency narrows those bounds to 2.7250–7.0450, still not a score, prediction or rankable midpoint. Q is final BQS, not a substituted subjective quality point. No governance or funding failure cap is applied without sufficient evidence of an actual failed gate. All three ranking-eligibility flags are false.

Factor audit records evidence, contrary facts, confidence and reasons. GOV/MOAT one-point changes move known BQS by.20; EARN moves GQS by.15 and P moves IAS by.10. Such judgment changes do not repair missing CAP/R/L. An improvement in cash conversion could remove the GQS cap only after the underlying persistence concern is resolved. Raw contributions, overrides and final NS are distinct.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Greenleaf designs, builds and commissions water and wastewater treatment facilities, including STP/ETP work, and provides O&M, environmental testing/advisory and fire-safety services. Revenue is principally project execution, not an annuity utility tariff. Engineering, procurement, outsourced inputs/subcontracting and milestone certification create recognized revenue before cash necessarily arrives. Government end-use does not mean the direct contractual debtor is the government or that collection is sovereign-guaranteed.

FY25 revenue categories were turnkey ₹33.1246 crore, O&M₹2.4862 crore, laboratory ₹1.7938 crore, environmental/legal services ₹1.1122 crore and fire ₹.3353 crore, summing ₹38.8521 crore. The FY26 presentation describes project work as about 94.7% of revenue. O&M contracts and laboratory relationships can improve recurring access, but are too small to characterize the entire business as recurring. A reliable gross-profit/value-added series separating subcontractor pass-through is ND; total revenue is not substituted with an aggregator's operating-profit measure.

The new wholly owned subsidiary is building a 10MLD CETP at Sayan. Management described a ₹35 crore project,60 members and bookings covering 2,500 of 4,000 machines, with ₹10 crore total membership funding and potential ₹.8 crore monthly revenue. These are management statements, not audited mature-plant unit economics. The original EPC business and prospective owned utility have different capital intensity, utilization, environmental liability and collection risks. Their revenues, margins and capex are therefore separated in the annual model.

FY25 Gujarat contributed about 74.1% of sales; the largest customer 12.4%, top five 50.4% and top ten 77.6%. Management characterized roughly 90% of projects as government-linked at the ultimate-owner level and about half of business as repeat, but these are not audited recurring-revenue percentages. Loss of one major client, retendering or delayed owner disbursement can materially change working capital even without losing reported revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism → evidence → durability → failure mode: delivery experience and qualifications support tender access; operation since 2010, executed projects and laboratory/O&M capabilities support that access; relationships may persist over repeat projects; price-led tenders, competing qualified engineers and poor collection economics can erode the benefit. A capable entrant needs engineering staff, references, compliance capability, guarantees and working capital, not an irreplaceable platform. The cost and time to replicate are material but not quantified sufficiently to establish a structural moat.

O&M and testing can create switching friction because plant knowledge and compliance continuity matter. Evidence is the disclosed revenue mix and existing operating capability, not proof of extraordinary pricing power. The failure mode is small recurring scale, retendering and customers splitting contracts. A proposed GAC-SBR patent application is not a granted patent or demonstrated royalty moat. Market share and a precisely defined accessible-market denominator are ND; no top-three or national-leader label is used.

Peer context is informative rather than a mechanical P/E screen. CRISIL's July 2026 Apex Ecotech rationale reports FY26 operating income ₹148.66 crore, PAT₹17.02 crore, adjusted debt/equity.02 and BBB/Stable/A3+; it describes improved collection and stronger liquidity. CRISIL's September 2026 Effwa rationale reports revenue ₹253.29 crore, PAT₹28.62 crore, adjusted debt/equity.31 and BBB+/Stable/A2. Both have greater scale, but different projects and credit profiles. These credit opinions are not audits or equity recommendations.

The prospectus also compares Felix, Apex and Effwa using earlier financials. Those are historical context, not current multiples. Apex FY25 PAT₹8.5608 crore in the issuer's peer table differs from ₹5.95 crore in the later CRISIL rationale, so their earnings bases cannot be mixed silently. No point-in-time peer valuation premium/discount is asserted without matching share counts, quotes and earnings definitions. Greenleaf's useful but contestable position merits MOAT5, not a bonus for an attractive industry narrative.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The preferred window was selected as five years before scoring. FY21 revenue ₹15.4892 crore to FY26₹60.6130 crore gives CAGR31.37%; FY23₹26.4104 crore to FY26 gives three-year CAGR31.91%. FY26 growth is 56.01%, an absolute ₹21.7609 crore increase. FY22 grew sharply, FY23 was approximately flat on final restated figures, then FY24/FY25/FY26 accelerated. No ten-year comparable series is available. Revenue expansion is not inferred from PAT margin growth.

The five-year endpoints span a pandemic-affected base and different restatement vintages. Earlier FY23 revenue ₹27.0470 crore versus final ₹26.4104 crore and original FY24₹32.9151 crore versus final ₹32.5032 crore remain unbridged at a detailed transaction level. The three-year cross-check is more relevant to recent scale, but still ends in first-year consolidation. The subsidiary contributed no operating sales, so consolidation does not itself explain the FY26 sales jump. No reliable quantitative price/volume/acquisition decomposition was found; growth is attributed cautiously to more project execution rather than a measured market-share gain.

H1FY26 revenue ₹21.0776 crore and PAT₹2.8820 crore imply H2FY26₹39.5354 crore and ₹4.3522 crore from audited full-year subtraction. That seasonality argues against multiplying one half-year by two. No H1FY27 financial release was available in the retrieved record by 20 October. FY26 is the latest full-year earnings anchor, not an invented September 2026 TTM.

June management backlog was ₹95 crore, with ₹80 crore expected FY27 and ₹15 crore later. The ₹25.5 crore Eiffil agreement includes GST and should neither be treated as net revenue nor automatically added to the same-date backlog. Secondary reports mention August order wins, but the underlying filings were not authenticated in this pass; their amounts are not used to inflate the executable backlog. The bidding pipeline and further plant aspirations are excluded from booked sales.

REV begins at 9 under the≥30% schedule, has zero net trajectory adjustment and is capped at 8 for Medium confidence. This is not a second penalty for a small absolute base. The cap reflects comparability and decomposition, not the mere fact of being recently listed.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Scale is not yet proof of self-funded per-share compounding. FY26 reported PAT₹7.2342 crore is mostly operating, but cash realization and new capital requirements diverge. The ₹35 crore CETP alone is more than half of quote market capitalization. The audited ₹3.4441 crore CWIP does not establish the timing or cash cost to finish. Management's 70% civil-completion statement refers to a construction component, not 70% of the full ₹35 crore cash commitment.

Three- and five-year observed incremental-return proxies are embedded with NOPAT changes, financing-derived IC changes, net fixed investment and a narrow operating-working-capital bridge. Their residual is shown rather than labelled reconciled operating investment. Broad IC includes non-operating deposit balances, restatements change the historical perimeter, and higher margins on older projects cannot be assigned to new capital. A reasoned nominal INR14–18% cost-of-capital range reflects a small, concentrated EPC/utility transition, collection risk and limited financeability. It is not the 15% equity hurdle mechanically relabelled as WACC. Neither a proxy above that range nor headline ROCE proves incremental value creation.

CAP remains NS because no mature CETP utilization, treatment revenue per unit, operating cost, maintenance capex, member refund terms or cohort-level cash return has been established. The base case tests ₹6 crore CETP revenue in FY28, then ₹9.6 crore FY29, with 32% EBITDA margin as an analyst assumption, not company guidance. Bull tests faster utilization and 40%; bear delays and limits uptake with 23%. At design capacity 10MLD,₹9.6 crore annual revenue implies about ₹26.30 per kilolitre at full 365-day utilization, or ₹32.88 at 80% utilization. Those are consistency checks, not disclosed tariffs.

EPC revenue paths begin FY27 at ₹62/80/92 crore in bear/base/bull, with subsequent growth, collection days, inventory, payables, maintenance capex and taxes linked annually. No acquisition or four-to-five-plant expansion is assumed without capital. Existing membership deposits are a financing claim, not operating earnings. Growth can be economically worthwhile only if margins survive collection costs, contract losses and dilution. CASH3 triggers the GQS cap based on repeated realization problems; CAP is not pushed to a low score simply because evidence is absent.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The founder-led structure brings operating continuity but related-party and financing concentration. FY26 director remuneration was ₹.48 crore versus ₹.24 crore in FY25, about 6.6% of reported FY26 PAT, plus disclosed related rent ₹.024 crore. Promoter interest-free financing increased to ₹2.4659 crore; receipts ₹3.7583 crore and repayments ₹1.9552 crore are support, not irrevocable permanent capital. September shareholding reports promoters 56.37%, no declared promoter pledge/other encumbrance, and about 74.2% of total shares locked. Locked stock is not freely executable float.

The 19 August warrants total ₹15.4 crore at ₹80: only 25%,₹3.85 crore, was received initially;₹11.55 crore is optional until 18 months after allotment. Conversion creates 1.925 million shares and 24.51% dilution of existing owners. Promoter participation is positive alignment evidence, but does not remove minority dilution or guarantee future cash. September's ₹1.99 crore subsidiary rights subscription is an internal group transfer, not new group financing. IPO funds were reported used according to the stated objects, including working capital and general corporate purposes; this does not by itself prove a return on deployment.

The statutory audit and internal financial-control opinions were unmodified. Secretarial observations include non-registration of charges for BMW/ICICI financing and the RBL facility. The board described BMW omission as oversight to be corrected, said an ICICI compounding application was filed 16 July 2025, and asserted the RBL charge filing was inapplicable because collateral belonged to individuals. These responses are retained, not independently endorsed as legal conclusions. M B Jajodia & Associates was reappointed for a further five-year term on 27 August 2026, not shown as resigning over access or information disputes. The 12 October SME governance-report exemption is a disclosure of applicability, not automatic misconduct.

Material contested proceedings require special care. The final prospectus describes a resolution professional's application concerning Jyoti Buildtech, seeking an FIR direction over alleged forged/unauthorized receipts of ₹2.8479754 crore. Greenleaf denies wrongdoing, calls the action malicious/duplicative and asserts legitimate work/payment claims and delayed deductions. FY26 contingencies separately show ₹1.5338 crore RP claim and ₹.9447 crore tax disputes; the RP amounts may overlap, so they are not simply added. The company contests the tax interpretation and says legal advice supports no material provision. No current merits order resolving the allegation was found. G1 is Hold, not a finding of fraud or GOV≤3 override.

Promises versus delivery: FY26 revenue expansion is delivered; the ₹15 crore April–May collection statement is management-reported but not independently confirmed;₹80 crore backlog execution in FY27 is a future target; March 2027 commissioning remains not yet due at cutoff. No invented missed deadline is charged against management. Required next evidence is customer receipts, project milestones and a funded completion plan, not another headline backlog number.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Audited FY26 consolidated revenue ₹60.6130 crore, operating EBITDA excluding other income ₹10.2406 crore, EBIT₹9.9861 crore, PAT₹7.2342 crore and CFO−₹13.0725 crore must be read together. Finance costs include ₹.1574 crore recurring bank fees; retaining them as operating expense gives EBITDA₹10.0832 crore and EBIT₹9.8287 crore. Removing all ₹.2794 crore other income at a normalized 25% tax rate gives PAT₹7.02465 crore. That conservative proxy is not a rewritten audited profit. The transcript's ₹12.52 crore EBITDA is inconsistent with audited arithmetic and its own growth percentage; the presentation also uses ₹10.5199 crore including other income. These definitions are reconciled rather than mixed.

Reported FY26 weighted EPS₹13.79 uses 5,245,459 shares; current-share EPS₹12.20 uses 5,929,250. Unchanged profit divided by full warrant shares gives ₹9.21. FY25 final restated EPS₹10.17 differs from statutory ₹9.95. Historical bonus/right-adjusted denominators are retained; no unadjusted old basic EPS is compared to post-bonus EPS. Gross profit is ND because a consistent separation from project/subcontractor costs is unavailable. No separate lease-debt schedule is assumed under AS; operating rent stays in operating expense. Inventory includes work in progress and is not duplicated as an extra contract asset.

The cash problem is not cash capex being incorrectly charged to CFO. Receivables absorbed ₹26.9381 crore in FY26, inventory released ₹1.2986 crore and group payables provided ₹2.5697 crore. CFO also includes ₹3.0857 crore membership deposits, so excluding that financing-like inflow gives−₹16.1582 crore. Standalone CFO is even weaker at−₹19.5022 crore. Consolidation introduces subsidiary payables/member funding and removes intercompany balances; different group and parent CFO totals are expected in principle, not an accounting error. The ₹6.4297 crore perimeter difference is material at 88.9% of group PAT. G2 Hold concerns the unresolved member-deposit/capital-creditor classification and historical restatement bridge, not the mere existence of that difference. It does not prove better EPC collections. Cash capex was ₹5.3160 crore, comprising PPE₹1.8346 crore, intangibles ₹.0373 crore and CWIP₹3.4441 crore. Reported CFO less capex is−₹18.3885 crore before interest classified as financing. Fiscal cash bridge: opening ₹2.5944−CFO₹13.0725−investing ₹5.1621+financing ₹18.9529=closing ₹3.3127 crore.

Closing receivable days are 233.7 against about 112 in FY25; average-balance days are 152.6 and must not be confused with closing days. Ageing from due date:₹28.8718 crore under 6 months,₹7.8520 crore 6–12 months,₹1.2028 crore 1–2 years,₹.0244 crore 2–3 years and ₹.1729 crore undisputed over 3 years, plus ₹.6925 crore disputed over 3 years. No provision is shown. The overdue-over 6 month subtotal ₹9.9446 crore is material even if most receivables eventually collect. Management's post-year-end ₹15 crore collection claim is the key contrary evidence, but not independently verified here.

Five-year comparison needs accounting discipline. Final restated FY24 CFO−₹.8391 crore differs from original statutory−₹3.0576; final FY25₹5.7473 differs from statutory ₹5.5917. Historical cash/FD/security deposit perimeters also differ. Each annual cash statement is reconciled to its own reported opening balance, not forced to match an inconsistent prior-vintage closing figure. The latest-three statutory ratio of CFO sums to PAT sums is-0.75×. Even the positive FY25 restated CFO relied on ₹6.4584 crore payable growth. This supports the persistent-realization assessment without claiming every negative year is fraud or a permanent write-off.

March cash availability: reported equivalents ₹3.3127 crore less ₹.6549 crore designated IPO balance and ₹.9230 crore unverified short-FD availability leaves conservative ₹1.7348 crore. Liberal equivalent cash is ₹2.6578 crore. Other current bank balances ₹.2873 crore, non-current bank deposits ₹.9443 crore and operating security deposits are not automatically saleable excess cash. Gross external group debt ₹6.7078 crore is distinct from standalone ₹9.5981 crore, which includes ₹2.8903 crore internal debt. Member deposits ₹3.0857 crore remain separate claims pending contract review.

The model pays legacy net income tax ₹1.1232 crore once (₹2.5061 provision less ₹1.3829 TDS asset), with a gross-tax/no-credit stress, and gratuity ₹.1860 crore once. It does not repay the historical ₹.802089 crore IPO-funded tax use a second time. Subsidiary payables ₹3.9958 crore are conservatively separated as presumed capital creditors pending ledger verification; this changes classification, not duplicated consolidated debt. A template note says no CWIP despite ₹3.4441 crore on the balance sheet, another reason to reconcile notes rather than assume text perfection.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹117.80,5,929,250 shares imply ₹69.846565 crore equity value. On current shares, FY26 reportedP/E is 9.66×, normalizedP/E9.94× andP/B2.00×. AddingMarch gross debt and deducting conservativeMarch usable cash gives EV/normalized operating EBITDA7.42×. This is explicitly a mixed-date diagnostic, not verifiedOctober enterprise value. The ₹136 IPO price is historical, not intrinsic value support. A small market cap creates possible upside, not an investment case.

The five-year annual model separates EPC and CETP, with receivable/inventory/payable assumptions, other operating capital, cash taxes, maintenance and growth capex, interest, debt repayment, membership funding and equity. FY27 begins with an auditedMarch 2026 balance, a pro forma pre-entry bridge to 19 October and a post-entry stub to 31 March 2027. FY28–31 are full fiscal years, followed by actual-day FY32 cash flows only to 19 October 2031. Terminal EBITDA is trailing twelve months across FY31/FY32 daily fractions, not a full FY32 number recognized early. No dividends are assumed.

Bear/base/bull EPCFY27 sales are ₹62/80/92 crore; EBITDA margins 12/16/18%; receivable days 230/180/140; exit EV/EBITDA6/9/12×. CETP revenue, margin, build-cost and membership schedules are separately explicit. Base project capex afterMarch is ₹31.5559 crore; bear assumes a cost overrun/delay, bull earlier spending. Maintenance is an estimate of 1.2% EPC sales plus 3% CETP sales, not depreciation relabelled as cash maintenance. Existing bank debt is rolled only at its observed level, not an invented sanction headroom. Promoter debt is paid FY29 in the model. Monthly troughs remain untested, so annual solvency is not proof of financeability.

All six non-rescue cases fail the cash floor of max(₹1.5 crore,3% annual revenue). Accordingly their conditional IRRs and entry prices are also null. The base non-rescue case assuming warrant exercise has peak floor deficit ₹15.18 crore. This is a scenario funding requirement, not a verified actual default. The optional ₹11.55 crore warrant payment is assumed within FY28 before its deadline; accelerated FY27 conversion is tested separately. The ₹3.85 crore upfront is included once before entry and no new shares are credited until conversion. A balance arriving later cannot cure an earlier cash trough without bridge funding.

Rescue cases are explicitly hypothetical third-party equity at ₹50/80/95 with 3% fees, and the quoted investor does not subscribe. Base plus warrants needs gross rescue ₹15.64 crore and fees ₹0.47; its conditional nominal IRR is 15.7%. This narrow proximity to the 15% hurdle is not a margin of safety because funding, price and operating assumptions are unverified. Bear and bull rescue outputs,12/15/18% hurdle entry sensitivities and DSO/multiple/capex/delay stresses are tabulated below and fully embedded in the model. No probability-weighted expected return is manufactured.

Terminal enterprise value includes productive property and the CETP; these assets are not added again. Only cash above the operating floor is distributable. Remaining group debt, membership claims and unpaid legacy obligations are deducted once. Existing IPO money, internal subsidiary rights, already received warrant cash, prepayments, TDS and restricted deposits are not separate terminal windfalls. A DCF is not used to disguise funding uncertainty. Ordinary entry/return outputs remain null even where a rescue illustration clears the hurdle.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The permanent-loss path is a sequence, not just a lower exit multiple: owner/client payments delay; certified revenue remains in receivables; working-capital borrowing and supplier credit stop expanding; CETP invoices fall due before member/warrant funding; project completion slips; equity must be raised at a discount or assets/claims are impaired; concentrated, illiquid shares then prevent a clean exit. A tax/RP loss could accelerate the same process. Outstanding guarantees/LC₹1.8858 crore are contingent trade exposures, not automatically added to debt and then counted as a loss again.

The bear operating case uses weaker EPC growth and 12% margin,230-day receivables, delayed CETP receipts,23% CETP margin and ₹38.4441 crore total project cost rather than ₹35 crore. It tests a ₹3.7926754 crore combined maximum RP-alleged-receipt-plus-tax loss; this uses the larger RP amount, not both potentially overlapping RP claims. Company denials and pending adjudication mean this is a stress, not an expected liability. Receivable impairment is economically distinct from reported collection timing, but a detailed recoverability probability cannot be assigned without customer-level evidence.

Without rescue the model is not funded; it does not continue treating a negative cash balance as financing while publishing an investible IRR. Rescue cases separately issue shares and pay fees, so loss absorption falls on existing owners even if the business survives. Approximate book equity ₹34.8688 crore provides accounting cushion, but much of the asset base is receivables, operating deposits and an unfinished plant rather than cash. Subtracting a generic book-value haircut is not a substitute for this claim-by-claim analysis.

Contrary evidence matters: operations have scaled, reported profits are predominantly operating, management reports collections, promoter financing has supported the company, and warrants can add capital if exercised. No current default, cash diversion or adjudicated fraud was established. That prevents an automatic governance-failure or distressed-funding cap. It does not justify dismissing the funding gap or assuming a liquid exit at the last traded quote.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold wealth over five years require annualized returns of 37.97% and 58.49%, far above the 15% hurdle. Small starting market capitalization alone does not make these outcomes plausible. The relevant numerator is terminal equity per current shareholder after dilution, not group revenue or total market capitalization.

Reverse expectations use the base rescue terminal share count and explicit terminal cash, debt and membership claims. For 6/9/12× exit EBITDA, the model solves the EBITDA required to deliver 2.01136× wealth (15% for five years),5× and 10×, then translates that EBITDA into illustrative revenue at 16% margin. This is a requirement table, not a growth forecast. Its fixed financing assumptions must be rerun if target scale changes, because more sales can require more receivables, guarantees, plant capital and shares.

At the base plan, existing EPC projects and one CETP do not establish a funded tenfold path. Higher CETP utilization or additional plants could increase earnings, but management's multi-plant ambition lacks verified funding and unit returns. Counting future plants without their capital costs or carrying today's share count through a large equity programme would artificially manufacture multibagger returns. A bull rescue case can show high conditional upside under strong margins, collections and a 12× exit multiple, but that is not evidence those conditions will coexist.

Evidence needed to promote optionality into a thesis: sustained cash realization, signed customer tariff/volume contracts, commissioned-plant costs and throughput, post-tax incremental returns exceeding the 14–18% cost-of-capital range, a realistic monthly financing bridge and per-share accretion after all warrants/new issues. Until those are available,5×/10× feasibility is speculative, not a valuation conclusion.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections first: reconcile the ₹38.8164 crore March receivables to the claimed ₹15 crore April–May receipts and a datedSeptember/October ageing. Identify receipts by invoice, retention, disputed balances and customer advances, not merely a lower headline debtor total. A positive cash conversion trend over two reporting periods, without payable stretching or new deposits masquerading as earnings, would change CASH and potentially remove the GQS cap.

2. Treasury and survival: obtain unrestricted bank balances, FD liens/maturities, renewal letters and actual available bank headroom; separate promoter loans, external bank debt and internal subsidiary transfers. Map monthly CETP invoices, member obligations and warrant payment dates to the required operating floor. Borrowing authorization or an unexercised warrant is not available cash. No ordinary entry price should be released before this bridge is credible.

3. CETP delivery: track remaining contracted cost, certified construction, approvals, March 2027 commissioning, actual throughput, realized tariff, operating cost, member refunds, environmental compliance and maintenance expenditure. Distinguish civil completion from full plant completion. Published operating cohorts, not a management margin aspiration, are needed to score CAP.

4. Governance: obtain current case-specific orders/settlements in the RP proceedings and tax appeals; resolve whether the ₹1.5338 crore claim and ₹2.8479754 crore alleged receipts overlap. Check charge-registration/compounding status against the board's explanations. Track related-party loans, compensation, warrants, exercise receipts, changes in share count and promoter encumbrances.

5. Disclosure quality: reconcile final prospectus versus statutory revenue/CFO and the EBITDA inconsistency. Obtain a subsidiary cash-flow and capital-creditor ledger to classify membership/capex funding. Review H1FY27 results when actually released, without treating an expected release date as reported data.

6. Implementation: confirm the four missing NSE dates and current lot/series/spread/depth. At ₹117.80 a ₹5 lakh ceiling permits 4lots/4,000 shares costing ₹4.712 lakh before costs;5lots cost ₹5.89 lakh and exceed that ceiling. The median 5,000-share observed day cannot support even one 1,000-share lot at 2%,5% or 10% participation. No trading or scheduled monitoring action is being placed by this analysis.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: speculative growth opportunity; Hold for funding, capital-return and legal evidence. This is not a verified self-funded compounder, a numerical Avoid-governance finding, or an immediately implementable value purchase. Revenue growth is strong, but the owned-plant transition and receivables make cash and share-count economics decisive.

BQS NS, GQS NS, IAS NS. GQS is Growth Quality, not a different governance score. Missing-data bounds are mathematical disclosures only. G1/G2/G3 Hold and G4 Conditional prevent a clean investible conclusion; ranking eligibility remains false. The 15% nominal five-year hurdle is applied only to explicitly financed sensitivity illustrations and does not supply a substitute ordinary price target.

The next decision is conditional on evidence rather than a price tick. A dated, funded operating bridge and confirmed collections could make current valuation worth revisiting. Attributable CETP returns and per-share cash progress could improve the quality thesis. Adverse court findings, persistent uncollected debtors, capex overruns or punitive financing would weaken it. Because ordinary returns and entry prices are null, no price is labelled a buy zone, no position size is recommended and no purchase is authorized or executed.

This is research rather than individualized investment advice. Illustrative ₹5 lakh lot arithmetic is an implementation constraint, not a portfolio recommendation. Reported data can be revised, forward assumptions can fail and SME shares can be difficult or impossible to exit at a displayed price.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Evidence hierarchy prioritizes NSE/company filings, audited annual statements, final prospectus and direct management disclosures. The earlier draft is used only for older history with its vintage disclosed. CRISIL peer rationales are primary credit opinions used for limited peer context, not company audits or price targets. Secondary screens were used to discover documents, not to replace authenticated financial statements. Original PDFs, rendered statement pages and file hashes underpin financial checks; retained analytical extracts alone do not authenticate an original source.

The source register records dates, URLs, SHA256 values where original files were retrieved, and page/section locations. The 60-session archive register independently lists each official archive hash. Peer web pages unavailable to direct download have no invented original checksum; their limited status is explicit. Source-free analytical copies preserve financial extracts, model code, results, URLs and hashes, not raw issuer PDFs, OCR, screenshots or personal identifiers. Reproducing arithmetic from those copies is not fresh source verification.

Open questions, ranked by economic importance: (1) ActualOctober cash/FD availability, collection receipts and sanctioned headroom. (2) Remaining CETP contractual cost and funding timing, including membership refundability and warrant exercise. (3) Detailed revenue/CFO restatement bridges and subsidiary capital-creditor classification. (4) Current merits/status/overlap of RP and tax proceedings. (5) Mature plant unit economics and incremental-return attribution. (6) Current executable orderbook, missing-session trading status and broker restrictions. (7) A fully reconciled current backlog including cancellations, GST, owner-payment terms and unexecuted orders.

Assumptions include 25% normalized tax,14–18% nominal cost-of-capital range,15% shareholder hurdle, recurring bank fees retained in operations, separate operating cash floor, no automatic value for restricted deposits/property beyond the enterprise model, no unverified borrowing capacity and explicit rescue fees/dilution. No missing observation is assigned zero and no missing factor receives a disguised midpoint. Cutoff is 20 October 2026. The analysis may be updated only when dated evidence changes, and conditional scenarios must not be quoted as forecasts or ordinary entry values.

evidence.title: Identity, quote and shares
facts: The exact ISIN matches Greenleaf Envirotech Limited on the official NSE records.
The 19 October close is ₹117.80, issued shares 5,929,250 and board lot 1,000.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: A traded close is not an executable offer or liquidation price.
evidence.locations: Prospectus cover; September shareholding; ISIN-filtered master and19October archive.

evidence.title: Revenue scale and basis
facts: Revenue is ₹15.4892 crore in FY21 and ₹60.6130 crore in FY26.
FY23 and FY24 revenue differs between older and final restatement vintages; the bases are labelled.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: A pandemic base, restatement differences and absent volume/price decomposition reduce comparability, despite substantial absolute growth.

evidence.title: Cash realization and funding-like operating receipts
facts: FY26 consolidated CFO is−₹13.0725 crore; standalone CFO is−₹19.5022 crore.
Reported consolidated CFO includes ₹3.0857 crore membership deposits; FY25 restated CFO benefited from ₹6.4584 crore payable growth.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Management reports ₹15 crore of April–May collections. No bank or customer confirmation was found; expansion capex itself does not explain negative CFO.

evidence.title: Receivables and ageing
facts: Receivables increased from ₹11.8803 crore to ₹38.8164 crore, outpacing revenue.
Overdue balances older than six months total ₹9.9446 crore, including ₹.6925 crore disputed over three years, without a shown provision.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: The company cites government-linked timing and subsequent collections. Those explanations do not guarantee recoverability of every invoice.

evidence.title: Business mix and contestable advantage
facts: FY25 turnover is dominated by ₹33.1246 crore turnkey projects; O&M and laboratory services are smaller.
Top five customers contribute 50.4%, top ten 77.6% and Gujarat 74.1% of FY25 sales.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Repeat relationships and lab/O&M expertise help customer access, but certifications and backlog do not by themselves establish pricing power.

evidence.title: Backlog and contract economics
facts: Management described June backlog of ₹95 crore, including ₹80 crore planned FY27 execution.
The ₹25.5 crore Eiffil agreement includes GST and collection depends on owner payments to the client.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Bidding pipeline is not revenue. No complete opening backlog plus intake less execution/cancellations bridge was available.

evidence.title: CETP future capital commitment
facts: The planned 10MLD CETP has a management budget of ₹35 crore and potential monthly revenue ₹.8 crore.
Audited CWIP is ₹3.4441 crore and received membership deposits ₹3.0857 crore; the total membership target is ₹10 crore.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Management says 70% of civil work was completed, not 70% of total capital cost paid. Commissioning and economics remain prospective.

evidence.title: Cash availability and liabilities
facts: Cash equivalents total ₹3.3127 crore, including ₹.6549 crore designated IPO cash and ₹.9230 crore short FD whose availability is not confirmed.
Group debt is ₹6.7078 crore, including ₹2.4659 crore promoter loans and ₹4.0947 crore revolving bank debt.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Equity and promoter support are buffers; March balances do not confirm October usable liquidity.

evidence.title: IPO and intra-group funding
facts: Net fresh IPO funds are ₹15.2267 crore after ₹2.5893 crore expenses;₹4.08 crore OFS is excluded from issuer funds.
September subsidiary rights funding ₹1.99 crore is internal;₹2.8903 crore intercompany debt is eliminated in consolidation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: No IPO-use deviation is reported. Deployment, including permitted tax use within GCP, does not prove economic return.

evidence.title: Warrants and dilution
facts: The 1,925,000 warrants have an ₹80 issue price, with ₹3.85 crore upfront and optional ₹11.55 crore balance.
Full exercise increases shares to 7,854,250, diluting existing ownership by 24.51%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Promoter participation supports alignment, but the remaining payment is optional, not a sanctioned cash facility.

evidence.title: Audit observations and company answers
facts: FY26 statutory and internal-control opinions are unmodified; no adverse auditor resignation was established.
The board gave specific oversight, compounding and collateral explanations for charge-registration observations.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: The legal sufficiency and final closure of each charge matter are not independently verified. The company responses are retained rather than treated as adverse findings.

evidence.title: Contested RP allegations and tax claims
facts: A prospectus-disclosed RP application alleges unauthorized receipts and forgery involving ₹2.8479754 crore and seeks FIR directions.
FY26 contingencies include ₹1.5338 crore RP and ₹.9447 crore tax claims; overlap is not independently resolved.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Greenleaf denies wrongdoing, calls the action malicious/duplicative and contests tax demands. No current merits decision establishing misconduct was located.

evidence.title: Related parties and minority economics
facts: Director remuneration increased from ₹.24 crore to ₹.48 crore; related rent is ₹.024 crore.
Promoter loan receipts are ₹3.7583 crore, repayments ₹1.9552 crore and closing interest-free balance ₹2.4659 crore.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: September promoter encumbrances are declared nil; interest-free funding is supportive but not irrevocable equity.

evidence.title: Earnings normalization
facts: Audited arithmetic gives operating EBITDA₹10.2406 crore before reclassifying recurring bank fees.
After ₹.1574 crore recurring bank fees, normalized operating EBITDA is ₹10.0832 crore; normalized PAT proxy is ₹7.02465 crore.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Most profit is operating. Transcript EBITDA₹12.52 crore is inconsistent; the presentation also includes a differently defined ₹10.5199 crore figure.

evidence.title: Incremental economics not attributable
facts: Three- and five-year incremental NOPAT/capital proxies and investment-bridge residuals are shown.
Neither uncommissioned CETP investment nor margin improvements on old projects provide attributable returns on new capital.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Historical project margins are positive evidence of execution, but omit capital duration and collection economics needed for CAP.

evidence.title: Lot-aware tradability
facts: There are 56 issuer observations in 60 valid exchange sessions, with four unknown missing rows.
The 20-session observed median volume of 5,000 shares gives zero whole-lot capacity at 2/5/10% participation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Higher-volume days sometimes support a whole lot. Historical capacity and missing rows do not prove live executable depth.

evidence.title: Peer context
facts: CRISIL reports Apex FY26 revenue ₹148.66 crore, PAT₹17.02 crore and adjusted debt/equity.02.
CRISIL reports Effwa FY26 revenue ₹253.29 crore, PAT₹28.62 crore and adjusted debt/equity.31.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Different scale and mix limit comparability. Apex FY25 PAT differs between the issuer peer table and CRISIL, preventing an unqualified peer P/E comparison.

evidence.title: Annual financing scenarios
facts: Every modeled non-rescue case breaches the required operating cash floor.
Rescue cases issue new equity, deduct 3% fees, dilute shares and retain an operating cash floor at terminal.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: These are conditional analyst projections, not proof of actual default. Current funds and intra-year troughs remain unverified.

evidence.title: Disclosure scope and latest check
facts: The 12 October SME governance-exemption filing was retrieved from NSE.
The 27 August statutory-auditor filing is a reappointment, not an adverse resignation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: SME exemption is not misconduct. No claim is made that every later operational or legal event was captured.
